verdict.rationale: Smithery's token-scoping docs show scoped tokens tied to per-user metadata (e.g. a token limited to connections where metadata.userId is 'user-123'), and secure credential storage/automatic refresh are documented, which directly supports per-end-user credential isolation for a platform-engineer building on top of Smithery. However, there's no first-party documentation of a full per-user account management workflow (provisioning, revocation, auditing across many end users) beyond the single scoping example, and independent security research flagged real vulnerabilities (tool description injection, path traversal) that raise doubts about credential-boundary robustness in practice. missing for 10: dedicated multi-tenant/per-end-user account management docs beyond one scoping example, evidence of token revocation/rotation workflows at scale, and independent verification that scoped tokens hold up against the reported security findings.
